newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close below fresh record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close below fresh record.

text.p: French shares closed higher, but below a fresh historic high, after a rally underpinned by dollar strength and a rise on Wall Street, dealers said.

The market had started lower after an overnight fall on Wall Street on fears about what Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan would tell congress in the second part of his economic testimony. But early remarks on Wednesday about the market soothed investors fears.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 14.50 points or 0.55 percent at 2,666.19 after a high at 2,676.55 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,672 from 2,661 on Tuesday's close.
Dealers said investors were looking towards Thursday's German unemployment data and Friday's U.S. jobs data for further direction.
"We are mainly following the dollar," said a broker, noting the strength of the U.S. unit against the mark was good for exports and economic growth.
* Volume was 9.74 billion francs of which 7.13 billion in blue-chip shares.
* Alcatel Alsthom up 4.61 percent to 636 francs, helped by a recommendation by Robert Fleming, cost cuts at its German unit and fuelled by Thomson-CSF speculation.
* Seita closed down 1.75 percent at 213.60 francs with Societe Generale turning to "underperform" from "neutral" ahead of expected tobacco price reductions in France.

* Renault closes down 1.9 percent at 139.20 with dealers saying they did not like the intervention of the French government, seeking to soften a company decision to shut a plant in Belgium and cut jobs in France.

Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer is meeting Prime Minister Alain Juppe this evening with President Jacques Chirac having said that he was "shocked" about the method Renault used to announce its decisions.

* Thomson-CSF ended 1.55 percent higher at 196 francs after it reported a retrun to profit in 1996, after three years of losses. But the net figure, at 745 million francs, was below expectations while the operating result was in line.
* Pechiney, up 1.57 percent at 259 francs, Saint-Louis, down 0.40 percent at 1,483, and Casino, up 1.91 percent at 257 francs, are due to report year results on Thursday.
* Accor, up 3.10 percent to 799 francs, said it was selling an 11.5 percent stake in British company Compass.
